headline: House rejected a resolution that would have directed the President to remove U.S. troops from Venezuela unless Congress approved their use.
what_it_does: This resolution would have directed the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from Venezuela. The troops could have stayed only if Congress had passed a declaration of war or a specific authorization to use military force there. It was voted down in the House on January 22, 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the U.S. Armed Forces in Venezuela
who_it_affects.how: They would have been withdrawn from Venezuela unless Congress approved their presence.
The President would have been directed to pull U.S. forces out of Venezuela without approval from Congress.
Congress would have needed to pass a declaration of war or use-of-force authorization for U.S. forces to stay in Venezuela.
